recognitions.title: Three things that looked like resolutions this week all deferred the real question to later
recognitions.explanation: A ceasefire, a court ruling, and a shipping framework all landed this week wearing the shape of a resolution — and in each case, the people closest to it said out loud that the actual question is still open. A peace roadmap got its first verification mission, not a verified peace. A Supreme Court stay resolved a procedural fight while its own justices noted the underlying legality is untouched. A transit deal is 'in principle' and 'still being finalized.' Each is a real step. None of them is the thing a headline would make it sound like.

evidence.text: Russia lifted its quarantine Oct 8, with the governor saying nearly 5,000 tests found no dangerous microorganisms and declaring the matter resolved - but the one question the quarantine was actually about, whether the lab worker died of plague, is exactly as unconfirmed as it was on day one.

The Supreme Court's first argument of its new term looked like the system working through a hard question - but with Alito recused, legal commentators flagged a real chance of a 4-4 deadlock, which would resolve nothing and leave the preemption question exactly where it started.

Santa Cruz's civic leaders insist their demands don't include President Paz's resignation - just fuel imports and tax cuts. But their own Oct 10 deadline passed with no government response, and Evo Morales called his own supporters to protest starting today - a 'narrow' dispute now splitting into two fronts.

France's PM answered a month of school blockades with a letter deferring real decisions to 'fin octobre.' The Oct 13 strike that followed didn't resolve anything either - it just produced two numbers that can't both be right: the government counted 161,500 marchers, organizers say 480,000.
